"Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not."

1	# Case-study brief and source
2	
3	SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.
4	
5	## Brief
6	
7	Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.
8	
9	## Material
10	
11	Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.
12	
13	The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.
14	
15	Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:
16	
17	- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
18	- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
19	- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”
20	
21	Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.
22	
23	## Forbidden inferences / judging
24	
25	No claim that software caused the shorter assignment time, saved money, delighted residents or rescued a helpless customer. Do not turn assignment time into completion time. The customer's reservation must survive. Judge whether quotations contribute experience beyond the surrounding narrative, whether supplier narration stays in third person and whether the suggested link accurately describes its destination.

1	# Quoting speech
2	
3	Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.
4	
5	Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.
6	
7	When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.
8	
9	## What may be repaired
10	
11	The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.
12	
13	That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.
14	
15	## What may not
16	
17	**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.
18	
19	**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.
20	
21	**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.
22	
23	**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.
24	
25	**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.
26	
27	**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.
28	
29	## When to paraphrase instead
30	
31	Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.
32	
33	The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.
34	
35	Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.
36	
37	## What stays outside this
38	
39	Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.

# Source-fidelity report: Elm Quay case (sv draft vs. en source)

Scope: I compared the complete draft (title, lead, headings, body, link sentence) with source.md. I left the byline out of scope as instructed. General editorial and mechanical review is also outside scope.

## A. Claim accounting

| # | Draft passage | Source passage (source wording) | Difference / test | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title: "Samlad vy över felanmälningar hjälper Elm Quays team" | Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us" | The source gives this only as Lind's own assessment, in a quotation. The title states it as a fact in the publisher's (Svale's) voice. See F1. | **Finding F1** |
| 2 | "Under åtta veckor provade Elm Quay Housing en gemensam logg för felanmälningar i två hus." | "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings"; "The trial lasted eight weeks." | The subject changes from the maintenance team to the company it belongs to. I found no case where one statement holds and the other fails. | Supported |
| 3 | "Arbetsledaren Maya Lind skulle göra om provet, men med en extra vecka för förberedelser." | "I would choose to do the trial again. ... but I would leave an extra week for preparation." | Stance, conditional mood and reservation are all kept. "Arbetsledaren" matches "maintenance supervisor". | Supported |
| 4 | "Här är hur underhållsteamet lade upp arbetet, vad mätningarna visar och vad de inte kan visa." | Trial note figures; "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software"; "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." | This is the author's own framing and rests on supported material. | Supported |
| 5 | "Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter." | "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats." | None. | Supported |
| 6 | "Tidigare sparades felanmälningar som kom in per telefon och per mejl var för sig." | "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." | The draft narrows "emails" to emailed fault reports. See F3. | **Finding F3** (minor) |
| 7 | "I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att prova en gemensam felanmälningslogg i två av husen." | "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." | "två av husen" implies the company has more buildings. Lind's "before the next building starts" supports that. | Supported |
| 8 | "Maya Lind, arbetsledare för underhållet, beskriver vad provet krävde och hur hon värderar det." | "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; the quotations; "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." | This is framing, supported by the quotations. | Supported |
| 9 | Heading: "Teamet bestämde kategorierna och Svale lade in dem" | "The maintenance team designed its categories"; Lind: "The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log." | "bestämde" is weaker than "designed" but still true. "Svale lade in dem" (Svale entered them) is stronger than "Svale helped us put them into the log". See F2. | **Finding F2** |
| 10 | "Innan underhållsteamet valde Svale Systems testade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation." | "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair." | Same sequence. The draft adds no causal link and implies no comparison with other suppliers ("No comparison with another supplier is available"). | Supported |
| 11 | "De boende kunde fortsätta att felanmäla per telefon." | "The maintenance team ... kept telephone reporting open for residents." | The draft does not say the team made this choice, but that omission makes nothing false. | Supported |
| 12 | Quote 1 + "skriver Maya Lind i en mejlintervju" | Quote 1; "All interviews occurred by email" | See section C for the translation check. The speech tag is supported. | Supported |
| 13 | "Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex anställda vid två tillfällen. Provet pågick i åtta veckor." | "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks." | None. | Supported |
| 14 | Heading: "Mediantiden blev kortare – orsaken lämnas öppen" | "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period." | The heading drops "from report to assignment". See F4. "orsaken lämnas öppen" is taken up under D. | **Finding F4** |
| 15 | "Enligt Elm Quays interna anteckning om provet, daterad den 4 december 2025, fördes 31 felanmälningar in i loggen. Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställdes före provet ingår inte." | "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." | The attribution, the date, the count and both exclusions are all kept. | Supported |
| 16 | "Mediantiden från felanmälan till att ärendet fördelades var två arbetsdagar under provet, mot tre under de åtta veckorna innan." | Same sentence as in row 14. | None. It stays assignment time and is not turned into completion time. | Supported |
| 17 | "Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden." | "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | None. | Supported |
| 18 | "Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var klara." | "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." | None. | Supported |
| 19 | Heading: "Arbetsledaren skulle göra om provet med mer förberedelse" | Quotes 2 and 3 | Stance and reservation are kept. | Supported |
| 20 | Quote 2 + "skriver Lind" | Quote 2 | See section C. | Supported |
| 21 | Quote 3 + "skriver hon om provet som helhet" | Quote 3; "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." | "om provet som helhet" characterises the quotation. The quotation's own content ("do the trial again") is an assessment of the whole trial, so this is defensible. | Supported |
| 22 | "Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger hon inte." | "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company." | The scope is kept: no universal recommendation, and no claim that she recommends Svale to nobody. The present tense sits inside the article's reporting frame. | Supported |
| 23 | Heading: "Teamet ska pröva kategorierna på större reparationer först" | "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | "först" is read against the body sentence that follows it ("fattar beslut om det när..."), so it means before deciding. It does not assert that the trial will expand. | Supported (see D) |
| 24 | "Provet har ännu inte utvidgats. Underhållsteamet fattar beslut om det när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer." | "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | None. | Supported |
| 25 | "Den som planerar ett eget prov kan läsa [checklistan för implementering](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist) innan planeringen börjar." | "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist ...; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." | The link is accurately described as a checklist to read. The rest is advice. | Supported |

Terms carried across languages:
- "felanmälan/felanmälningar" for "repair report(s)": both name reports of a repair need. I found no case in this context that falls under one term and not the other.
- "arbetsledare" for "supervisor": same.
- "anställda" for "staff": same.
- "akuta ärenden" for "emergencies": same.
- "hus" for "buildings": same.

## B. Pronoun accounting

- **"hon"** (lead paragraph and the paragraph after quote 3) refers to Maya Lind. It is third person singular and asserts female natural gender. The source supports this: "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment."
- **"det"** refers to "underhållsteamet" (rows 10 and 24, "testade det", "när det har sett"). It is third person singular with neuter grammatical gender and makes no natural-gender assertion. This matches the source's "It chose..." and "the team".
- **"det"** refers to "provet" ("hur hon värderar det") and to the expansion ("beslut om det"). Both are grammatical neuter only.
- **"de"** ("vad de inte kan visa") refers to "mätningarna" and **"dem"** (heading, row 9) refers to "kategorierna". Both are third person plural with no gender.
- **"vi/oss/våra"** in quotes 1–3 correspond to the source's "we/us/ours" (first person plural). **"jag"** corresponds to "I" (first person singular). Person and number are kept.
- **"Den som planerar"** is generic and asserts no gender.

## C. Translation of quotations

- **Q1:** "Kategorierna var våra egna" renders the stressed "ours" idiomatically and adds nothing. Splitting the semicolon into two sentences keeps the meaning. "Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem" keeps "helped". No obstruction.
- **Q2:** "komma överens om", "föra in", "avsätta den tiden" and "kommer i gång" are idiomatic. The comparison and the conditional "skulle" are kept. No obstruction.
- **Q3:** "en samlad vy" is a faithful rendering of "one view". "ge förberedelserna en vecka till" matches "leave an extra week for preparation". The conditional, the qualification ("men") and the stance are kept. No obstruction.

No translation findings.

## D. Observations (not defects)

- **"orsaken lämnas öppen" (heading, row 14).** In the article's own voice this is accurate: the draft assigns no cause. The source does not say whether the note names workload as the cause. The heading's passive does not assert that it does not, so this is defensible. If the editor wants the heading to state exactly what is known, "– anteckningen tillskriver inte programvaran skillnaden" would do it.
- **Supplier-published status.** The source says the case is "supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism". The draft makes no claim of independence, so nothing in the draft contradicts this. Whether to disclose the status is an editorial question outside this comparison.

## E. Findings (source support)

**F1. Title turns Lind's assessment into the publisher's factual claim.**
- Draft: "Samlad vy över felanmälningar hjälper Elm Quays team".
- Source: only Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us". There is no measurement of benefit ("There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements"), and the note "explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software".
- Case: Lind finds the single view helpful, but other team members do not, or no benefit is measurable. The source statement (Lind says it helps) holds; the title's unattributed claim fails. Nothing in the material excludes this.
- The article is published by the supplier, so the unattributed title reads as Svale asserting an effect.
- Repair: attribute it, e.g. "Arbetsledaren på Elm Quay: En samlad vy över felanmälningarna hjälper oss".

**F2. Heading makes Svale the one who entered the categories.**
- Draft: "Teamet bestämde kategorierna och Svale lade in dem".
- Source: "Svale helped us put them into the log"; "Svale configured the log".
- Case: Elm Quay's staff entered the categories themselves, with Svale guiding them. The source holds and the heading fails. "Svale configured the log" does not exclude this case.
- The error also moves an action from the customer to the supplier, although the brief asks for the customer to stay the acting party.
- Repair: "Teamet bestämde kategorierna och Svale hjälpte till att lägga in dem".

**F3 (minor). "emails" narrowed to emailed fault reports.**
- Draft: "felanmälningar som kom in per telefon och per mejl".
- Source: "telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
- Case: the separately stored emails included internal staff or contractor emails that were not fault reports. The source holds and the draft fails. No supplied statement excludes this.
- Repair: "Tidigare sparades telefonanmälningar och mejl var för sig."

**F4. Heading drops the scope of the median.**
- Draft heading: "Mediantiden blev kortare".
- Source: "Median time from report to assignment ..."
- The unqualified heading can be read as median repair (completion) time. The source says there are none: "There are no ... completion-time measurements". The brief also warns: "Do not turn assignment time into completion time." The base contract requires scope to be kept in headings.
- Case: completion time did not shorten, or was never measured, while assignment time did. The heading, read as completion time, fails.
- Repair: "Mediantiden till fördelning blev kortare – orsaken lämnas öppen".

## Completion status

Complete. Four source-support findings are unresolved in the draft: F1, F2, F3 (minor) and F4. There are no translation findings. Section D lists two editorial observations that are not defects.
